# _autosummary/plcstream2py.html.md

# plcstream2py

stream2py interface to Siemens S7 PLC data.

Two layers, from low to high:

- [`plcstream2py.raw_plc`](_autosummary/plcstream2py.raw_plc.html.md#module-plcstream2py.raw_plc): a thin wrapper over `python-snap7`. `PlcDataItem`
  describes one value to read from a PLC (area, word length, DB number, offset, and
  how to decode the bytes); `PlcRawRead` connects to a PLC and reads a list of them.
- [`plcstream2py.plc`](_autosummary/plcstream2py.plc.html.md#module-plcstream2py.plc): `PlcReader`, a `stream2py.SourceReader` that polls a
  `PlcRawRead` on a background thread so PLC readings can be consumed as a stream.

Both layers need `python-snap7`, which wraps the native `snap7` library, so they
are not imported here: `import plcstream2py` stays free of that dependency.

### Modules

| [`plc`](_autosummary/plcstream2py.plc.html.md#module-plcstream2py.plc)                   | A `stream2py` source reader for Siemens S7 PLC data.                            |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`raw_plc`](_autosummary/plcstream2py.raw_plc.html.md#module-plcstream2py.raw_plc)           | Thin, snap7-level access to values stored in a Siemens S7 PLC.                  |
| [`snap7_compat`](_autosummary/plcstream2py.snap7_compat.html.md#module-plcstream2py.snap7_compat) | One place that knows how `python-snap7` is laid out, across its major versions. |


# _autosummary/plcstream2py.plc.html.md

# plcstream2py.plc

A `stream2py` source reader for Siemens S7 PLC data.

[`PlcReader`](_autosummary/plcstream2py.plc.html.md#plcstream2py.plc.PlcReader) wraps `plcstream2py.raw_plc.PlcRawRead` in a
`stream2py.SourceReader`: opening it starts a background thread that polls the PLC
for a fixed list of [`plcstream2py.raw_plc.PlcDataItem`](_autosummary/plcstream2py.raw_plc.html.md#plcstream2py.raw_plc.PlcDataItem) values, and `read`
pops the readings that have accumulated since the last call.

Importing this module needs `python-snap7` (which wraps the native `snap7`
library); reading anything from it also needs a reachable PLC.

### Classes

| [`PlcReader`](_autosummary/plcstream2py.plc.html.md#plcstream2py.plc.PlcReader)(ip_address, \*, items_to_read, ...)   |    |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----|

### *class* plcstream2py.plc.PlcReader(ip_address, , items_to_read, rack, slot, tcp_port=102, sleep_time=1.0)

Bases: `SourceReader`

#### MIN_RETRY_WAIT_S *= 0.1*

Least wait (s) after a failed poll, so `sleep_time=0` cannot spin on errors.

#### close()

Close and clean up source reader.
Will be called when StreamBuffer stops or if an exception is raised during read and append loop.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### *property* info *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*

A dict with important source info. Default can be init_kwargs and open timestamp.

This info will be available in BufferReader after SourceReader has opened but any changes
made between open and close are not guaranteed to be visible. Any continuous status updates
should be included with read data instead.

* **Returns:**
  dict

#### key(data_item)

Converts data into a comparable value to sort by

* **Parameters:**
  **data** – the return value of the ‘read’ method
* **Return type:**
  `ComparableType`
* **Returns:**
  ComparableType

#### open()

Set up source to be read and set some source info affected by open time like the time of
open. Will be called in StreamBuffer immediately before first read.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### read(blocking=False, timeout=0)

* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)
* **Returns:**
  timestamp, plc info, read db items as key:value

#### *property* sleep_time_on_read_none_s *: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*

Sets default sleep time for StreamBuffer when it reads None from SourceReader.
Useful when you know the period between data points.

For example if data only comes once every 10 seconds,
it would be inefficient to try and read again every 0.1 seconds and get None up to 100 times
but every 10 seconds or even 1 second would be much more reasonable depending on the use
case. Not necessary if read is a blocking function that always returns a data point.

Default is None which delegates the sleep time to StreamBuffer’s default.

* **Returns:**
  Optional[Union[int, float]] number of seconds to sleep


# _autosummary/plcstream2py.raw_plc.html.md

# plcstream2py.raw_plc

Thin, snap7-level access to values stored in a Siemens S7 PLC.

[`PlcDataItem`](_autosummary/plcstream2py.raw_plc.html.md#plcstream2py.raw_plc.PlcDataItem) describes a single value to read – where it lives in the PLC
(area, word length, DB number, start offset, amount) and how to turn the bytes that
come back into a Python value. `PlcRawRead` connects to a PLC and reads a list
of those items in one multi-variable request.

It works with `python-snap7` 1.x, 2.x and 3.x: the names that moved between them
come from [`plcstream2py.snap7_compat`](_autosummary/plcstream2py.snap7_compat.html.md#module-plcstream2py.snap7_compat). [`plcstream2py.plc`](_autosummary/plcstream2py.plc.html.md#module-plcstream2py.plc) builds the
streaming interface on top of it.

### Functions

| [`get_byte`](_autosummary/plcstream2py.raw_plc.html.md#plcstream2py.raw_plc.get_byte)(_bytearray, byte_index)   | Get the boolean value from location in bytearray   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|

# _autosummary/plcstream2py.snap7_compat.html.md

# plcstream2py.snap7_compat

One place that knows how `python-snap7` is laid out, across its major versions.

`python-snap7` reorganised its public surface between 1.x and 2.x, and again made
the client pure-Python in 3.x:

| layout   | names                         | exceptions                         |
|----------|-------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| legacy   | `snap7.types` (`S7AreaDB`,    | `snap7.exceptions.Snap7Exception`, |
| (1.x)    | `S7WLBit`, …), `snap7.common` | `RuntimeError`                     |
| modern   | `snap7.type` (`Area`,         | `RuntimeError` (and, in 3.x,       |
| (2.x+)   | `WordLen`), `snap7.error`     | `snap7.error.S7Error`)             |

The rest of the package imports the names it needs from here, so supporting a new
`python-snap7` release means touching this module only. Everything is resolved at
import time from what is installed; `SNAP7_LAYOUT` says which layout won.

Reading is the one behavioural difference worth a seam. The legacy and 2.x clients
hand an array of `S7DataItem` to the native library’s multi-variable read, which
honours each item’s `WordLen` (a *bit* item addresses a single bit). The 3.x
client accepts the same array but reads every item as plain bytes, ignoring
`WordLen` – a bit item would silently return the byte at the bit offset – and its
typed `read_area(..., word_len=...)` mis-parses the bit and real answers a PLC
sends (it returns no data). So on the pure-Python 3.x client [`read_data_items()`](_autosummary/plcstream2py.snap7_compat.html.md#plcstream2py.snap7_compat.read_data_items)
reads plain bytes and does the bit extraction itself; everywhere else it uses
`read_multi_vars`.

The plain-byte reads go out together when the 3.x client has the dict-based
`read_multi_vars` (recognised by its `use_optimizer` attribute): its (experimental)
optimizer merges adjacent items and packs them into few PDUs. Older 3.x clients get
one round trip per item.

### Module Attributes

| [`WORD_LEN_BYTES`](_autosummary/plcstream2py.snap7_compat.html.md#plcstream2py.snap7_compat.WORD_LEN_BYTES)   | Bytes one element of a given word length occupies in an item's read buffer.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`read_data_items`](_autosummary/plcstream2py.snap7_compat.html.md#plcstream2py.snap7_compat.read_data_items)(client, items)   | Read an array of `S7DataItem` from `client`; return the array, filled in.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### plcstream2py.snap7_compat.WORD_LEN_BYTES *= {1: 1, 2: 1, 4: 2, 6: 4, 8: 8}*

Bytes one element of a given word length occupies in an item’s read buffer.
(`Real` is over-allocated – 8 rather than 4 – as it always was; harmless.)

### plcstream2py.snap7_compat.read_data_items(client, items)

Read an array of `S7DataItem` from `client`; return the array, filled in.

Each item’s `pData` buffer receives its bytes and `Result` its status code
(0 on success), as `Client.read_multi_vars` does. Returns `None` when the
multi-variable read reports a non-zero status; a failed per-item read raises,
as the client’s own errors do.
